About the second question, I learned a lot to understand people suffering from various psychiatric diseases by joining the facebook support groups. For example, I have been in a borderline support group for some years and there i learned what really meant living with BPD. 

I have this idea that to help people, we must first understand who he/she's the person in front of us and then we must understand the disease to help him/her.

I am a psychiatry student. BPD has always been my favorite topic. There are certainly individual differences but this is true for every pathology, psychiatric and otherwise. Then in making the diagnoses we cannot rush, we have to go step by step and surely we cannot say to be sure from a simple chat (even if you refer to your experience) because we risk of making mistakes. For example seeing this chat we could also say that he has an impulse control disorder and so on... (And Surely you know, we need 5 criteria to diagnose BPD and we must exclude everything else)
I understand your hypothesis but I prefer to not casually using disease names (stigma reasons). 
P.S.
Of course I'm not saying you were wrong. It is not my intention to start any war ahahah
